newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa, Telefonica de Espana in digital TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Televisa, Telefonica de Espana in digital TV deal.

text.p: Mexican media giant Grupo Televisa and Spain's Telefonica de Espana said Monday they have signed an accord to offer digital television services in Spain.

"Grupo Televisa announced Monday it signed an accord to form an association with Telefonica de Espana and other Spanish television channels to develop and operate a digital television system, direct to home (DTH) by satellite, in Spain," Televisa said in a statement.

Of the new company, Televisa, Radio Television Espanola and Antena 3 will have a 17 percent stake each, Telefonica de Espana will have 35 percent, Television de Catalunya six percent, TeleMadrid four percent, Canal 9 a two percent stake and Television de Galicia one percent.

Televisa said the DTH company would operate services in Spain during the first half of 1997 and eventually planned to offer a total of 70 channels. It did not say what timetable it meant by "eventually".
"Test transmissions are programmed to start next month," the Televisa said.

Televisa, along with the other Spanish channels, will provide and develop programming for the DTH company, while Telefonica de Espana will be in charge of the technical transmission of the service, Televisa said.
